doc.title: Mike Wofford interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998

chapter: Singers: Sarah Vaughan and Ella Fitzgerald
title: Ella Fitzgerald compared with Sarah, and Ella's stage nerves
summary: Ella needed more specific accompaniment than the bebop-minded Sarah, and was nervous backstage but fine once on stage.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: So you have to, to keep it interesting for everybody, you have to try to find interesting little switches on things and a new take on something. So that’s a challenge. When you’re doing new material all the time you don’t maybe even have the time to think about that kind of stuff. So it was great. Ella, who I worked with later, what can you say about Ella? I mean we all know how remarkable Ella Fitzgerald was. Ella was a different kind of singer. Ella was more specific in what she needed to hear behind her and wanted to hear. And it was great too, it was just a different kind of thing. It was more tailoring what you do to make what she needed happen and work. Sarah was more of a bebopper in that sense. And of course when you understand the history of her early years it’s understandable, I mean coming up with the people she did.
Right. Was Ella’s — I had read that she tended to be, even as great as she was, quite nervous about coming on stage.

Yes, she was. She was. If Sarah was, she hid it very well. I was never ever aware of any nervousness. You never know for sure what’s going on inside someone, but Ella was like I think many accomplished actors and actresses and singers, and even people who’ve done it for decades talk about how nervous they are before they go out. Lawrence Olivier or someone talking about that they still get butterflies you know. I believe when he was still alive I think I remember hearing that comment in one interview from him. You can’t imagine that this person would still get butterflies. But Ella did. But then the minute she hit the stage, which is often the case with performers, that was gone and she was fine. I never sensed a moment’s lack of self assurance or any stage nerves once she hit the stage. But she’d be pacing around back stage before they announced her. And that’s really more typical I think than Sarah. Sarah was very unusual in not having that.
